reason: E1 reports that IrOsPtPdRhRu catalyzes a 12-electron ethanol oxidation process, but explicitly cautions that the d-band center theory may not describe HEA activity due to surface heterogeneity. E2 shows charge transfer to Pt/Pd and isolated sites in a different HEA (PtPdCoCuNi) for a different reaction, providing only indirect, loosely related support. The key premises about a ligand-driven d-band shift governing ethanol oxidation and the effect of hydrogen annealing are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Uniform alloying in PtPdRhRuIrOs creates isolated, electronically optimized Pt/Pd sites via a ligand effect.
This ligand effect shifts the d-band center of noble metal sites, enhancing ethanol adsorption and activation.
The shifted d-band center promotes a 12-electron complete ethanol oxidation pathway.
Mild hydrogen annealing removes surface oxides and further fine-tunes the d-band center.
The annealed catalyst will show higher current density and selectivity vs. the as-synthesized catalyst.
